Hi there Luiza.

First of all, did you follow the procedure from the CS training related to fraud price reviews and discussed this case with your TL and with OPS before creating this escalation? 

!PR workflow.png|width=463,height=680!

About the ride itself, I think you misunderstood the decision that was made from our side. We didn’t refund this ride because we thought they were done without the passenger inside the car. From the route points visible in the system, we know the driver did the kilometers. That’s not the point. We’ve refunded because this ride wasn’t logged/approved in the App. The ride request had a really low prediction and there’s no destination change logged/approved in the App to justify the route the driver made. If the payment were successful, refund wouldn’t happen from our side. So even if the ride was empty, if we collected the money, would stay like that until the customer complained and CS would do a usual refund.

Please be careful with your interpretation. This ride is fraudulent. The rider account was created on the day before and the payment method is intentionally a bad one that returned a permanent payment error (meaning we won’t be able to retry it). Please don’t compensate the driver this amount back.

We are covered by the [TOS|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/rs/terms-for-drivers/]:
{{6.5. We are not obliged to pay you the Fare due from the Passenger if the In-app Payment failed because Passenger's credit card or other payment is cancelled or is unsuccessful for other reasons.}}

Drivers have to be educated that if the passenger requests a new destination, they have to log that in the App and wait for approval. If we don’t approve the change, they have to follow the message that is displayed to them in the App (screenshot)

!Screenshot 2022-07-18 at 13.29.27.png|width=388,height=817!

So for these cases with low predictions and no destination change, we’ll always try to collect the money. But if the payment fails, we’ll refund it and drivers shouldn’t be compensated when we make this decision to refund.

Could there be something that may have caused it to switch or something we can tell to the customer? User has waited for a very long time. Tech support did not have any kind of specific information on it either.

Communicating car lease options should be deemed service-related (i.e. doesn’t require prior consent) and therefore won’t be classified as 3rd party marketing, which usually has a higher compliance threshold. if data sharing is in scope, then only data of data subjects who would be reasonably interested in the offer (e.g. prospect drivers that declared that they currently don’t have a car) should be disclosed.

During the meeting we went over the proposed marketing approach:
Similar to what was done in Poland as described by @dominika.pek and @Paweł Pyrlik, where a similar initiative was explored, it was agreed that Bolt will run the ads, without mentioning the details of the partner.
In this case, the interested car owners will be required to complete a form (majorly KYC details) with their name, phone number and email address. These details will then be aggregated on a google sheet and shared with MyGarage, who will then proceed to call these leads and complete their onboarding onto their platform.
@adriana.sokolska further confirmed from a data protection stand point that we will not be exposed to any liability, should we adopt the aforementioned process and ensure that a disclaimer is included where we mention that these details will be shared with a 3rd party. [~accountid:5b18f5574bec0e53fdb555d5]{color:#ff5630} +*some notes for you please*+{color}{color:#ff5630}: {color}I understand this is a rather unusual set up but I have discussed this with [~accountid:6017bc19dc29b4006a7f1025] and hopefully this is also fine with you - explanations below:

* This +*Bolt Car Program contract*+ is primarily between Bolt Operations OU and a driver and here it what is does: 

1. it defines the mechanism of a ‘*Bolt Car bonus*’ that we will be paid to the driver if he meets certains conditions (Bonus = EUR 3 per drive for any drive between 30 and 90 drives per week); and 

2. it contains a *direct payment authorization/mandate* whereby the driver instructs Bolt to pay his bonus (whatever the amount might be every week) in his name and on his behalf directly to Moov In Cab, a car leasing company, as partial payment of the car rental price that the driver owes to Moov In Cab.

* +A few more details+:
** Bolt’s obligations in this contract are very limited: i.e. if there is a Bolt Car bonus (it depends if the driver makes at least 30 rides in a week), then our sole obligation is to pay it to the car leasing entity. It is clearly stated that: 1. there is no carry over or accumulation of that bonus from one week to the next ; 2. no bonus shall be due if the Driver's account is inactive or suspended and 3. Bolt cannot be held responsible for any obligation under the car leasing contract (including payment of the car rental price). 
** It’s a 6-months contract, renewable once - we went for a short term contact so we can assess the benefits and also to balance the additional reclassification risks that such contract could present (_for further details on this, please see my post below dated 7th Feb_). 
** [~accountid:5b76bc2cb974540708ee16ee] agreed to limit this contract to 500 drivers to start with, to limit the reclassification risks.
** The car leasing company is also party to the contract with the driver; though they have no obligations in this contract, it’s just to make sure the contract will be enforceable against them and they know that a part of the car rental price will be paid by a third party (i.e. Bolt).
* +What’s unusual about it+: a contract needs to be signed +*with each driver*+, which means we’ll potentially need about 500 contracts signed by Bolt Ops OU and the drivers who want to participate.
* +How we propose to deal with this+: it seems that the easiest way would be to re-use the copy signed by [~accountid:5b18f5574bec0e53fdb555d5] , i.e. *Ahto signs one contract and then the RH team in Paris (*[~accountid:611bc3aeaee32f006f907fbc] ) *prints a number of copies and have them countersigned by the drivers who wants to enter into such arrangement with Bolt*. 

➡️  Considering the nature of this contract and Bolt’s limited obligations, I trust this approach is satisfactory but of course let me know [~accountid:5b18f5574bec0e53fdb555d5] should you wish to discuss this further 🙂 

* There’s also a +partnership agreement between Bolt and the car leasing company+ - but it has very limited obligations for Bolt and only needs to be signed once 😉

{noformat}-- use existing order_order_all_states_together in looker_scratch.LR$68W3E1658081866017_order_order_all_states_together
-- use existing provider_provider in looker_scratch.LR$68CDD1658130661815_provider_provider
SELECT
    CASE
        WHEN ('Hour' = 'Week') THEN (TO_CHAR(DATE_TRUNC('hour', CONVERT_TIMEZONE(admin_system_city.timezone,order_order.created) ), 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24'))
        WHEN ('Date' = 'Week') THEN TO_CHAR((DATE(CONVERT_TIMEZONE(admin_system_city.timezone,order_order.created) )), 'YYYY-MM-DD')
        WHEN ('Week' = 'Week') THEN (TO_CHAR(DATE_TRUNC('week', CONVERT_TIMEZONE(admin_system_city.timezone,order_order.created) ), 'YYYY-MM-DD'))
        WHEN ('Month' = 'Week') THEN (TO_CHAR(DATE_TRUNC('month', CONVERT_TIMEZONE(admin_system_city.timezone,order_order.created) ), 'YYYY-MM'))
        WHEN ('Quarter' = 'Week') THEN (TO_CHAR(DATE_TRUNC('month', DATE_TRUNC('quarter', CONVERT_TIMEZONE(admin_system_city.timezone,order_order.created) )), 'YYYY-MM'))
        WHEN ('Year' = 'Week') THEN CAST((DATE_PART(year, CONVERT_TIMEZONE(admin_system_city.timezone,order_order.created) )::integer) as char(4))
      END  AS "order_order.dynamic_timeframe",
    COUNT(DISTINCT order_order.id ) AS "order_order.count_of_orders",
    ( COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN ((1.0*datediff(seconds,order_order_all_states_together.provider_accepted, order_order_all_states_together.provider_waiting_for_pickup)/60) - (CASE WHEN order_order_all_states_together.disable_estimation_correction THEN order_order_all_states_together.provider_mm_cooking_time_plus_delay ELSE (1.0*datediff(seconds,order_order_all_states_together.provider_accepted, order_order_all_states_together.provider_ml_estimated_adjusted_time)/60) END)) > 5 THEN order_order_all_states_together.order_id END  ) )*1.0/nullif(( COUNT(*) ),0)  AS "order_order_all_states_together.percent_orders_with_cooking_time_delay_5_minutes"
FROM
    "delivery"."delivery_order_order" AS "order_order"
    LEFT JOIN "public"."admin_system_city" AS "admin_system_city" ON "order_order"."city_id" = "admin_system_city"."id"
    LEFT JOIN "public"."admin_system_country" AS "admin_system_country" ON "admin_system_city"."country_code" = "admin_system_country"."code"
    LEFT JOIN "looker_scratch"."lr$68w3e1658081866017_order_order_all_states_together" AS "order_order_all_states_together" ON "order_order"."id" = "order_order_all_states_together"."order_id" AND "order_order"."city_id" = "order_order_all_states_together"."city_id"
    LEFT JOIN "looker_scratch"."lr$68cdd1658130661815_provider_provider" AS "provider_provider" ON "order_order"."provider_id" = "provider_provider"."id"
WHERE ((( CONVERT_TIMEZONE(admin_system_city.timezone,order_order.created)  ) >= ((DATEADD(week,-2, DATE_TRUNC('week', DATE_TRUNC('day',GETDATE())) ))) AND ( CONVERT_TIMEZONE(admin_system_city.timezone,order_order.created)  ) < ((DATEADD(week,2, DATEADD(week,-2, DATE_TRUNC('week', DATE_TRUNC('day',GETDATE())) ) ))))) AND "provider_provider"."name_english" = 'KFC Kristiine Keskus' AND ("admin_system_city"."name" LIKE '%%' OR "admin_system_city"."name" IS NULL) AND ("admin_system_country"."name" LIKE '%%' OR "admin_system_country"."name" IS NULL)
GROUP BY
    1
ORDER BY
    1 DESC
LIMIT 500{noformat}

Täiendavalt PZU poolt 11.07.22 esitatud päringus toodule ja Teie alltoodud vastusele selgitame lisaks, et antud juhul tugineb PZU andmete küsimisel liikluskindlustuse seaduse (LKindlS), võlaõigusseaduse (VÕS) ja kindlustustegevuse seaduse (KindlTS) asjakohastele sätetele.

Vastavalt VÕS §-dele 488 ja 489 tekib kindlustusjuhtumi toimumisel kindlustusandjal kohustus välja selgitada juhtumi asjaolud ja kahju suurus. LKindlS § 38 lg 4 kohaselt VÕS §-is 488 sätestatud kahju ärahoidmise ja vähendamise ning kahju kindlakstegemise võimalikkuse tagamise kohustust kohaldatakse nii sõiduki omaniku, sõiduki vastutava kasutaja, kindlustusvõtja, sõiduki juhi kui ka kahjustatud isiku suhtes.

LKindlS § 53 lg 1 p 2 alusel tekib kindlustusandjal tagasinõude õigus sõidukijuhi vastu, kui sõidukijuht on põhjustanud kindlustusjuhtumi ja lahkus pärast kindlustusjuhtumit õigusvastaselt ja süüliselt kindlustusjuhtumi toimumise kohalt. Hey [~accountid:5eda5ad54ec4270ba37d2e87] the refunds will go back to the business balance (which is a different concept vs Bolt Balance). In this case looks like they’re credit card company so yes you’re correct - the money isn’t sent back to the CC but the next order(s) will be covered by the refunded amount. Let’s take this order [https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/rentals-carsharing/orders/edit/global/3838602?tab=details|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/rentals-carsharing/orders/edit/global/3838602?tab=details] as an example. 

!Screenshot 2022-07-19 at 15.31.16.png|width=1185,height=166!

So usually each order/claim is followed by the capture from CC/topup. The refund was processed on the 21st June so reading from the bottom-up:

* They took one ride on 21/06/2022, 15:50 for 1.99 EUR
* CC was charged on 21/06/2022, 15:53 for 1.99 EUR (the same amount)
* Now a refund was processed on 21/06/2022, 16:02 for 1.99 EUR
* The next ride was taken on 21/06/2022, 16:10 for 5 EUR
* But the CC was charged on 21/06/2022, 16:20 for 3.01 EUR (5 - 1.99)

Hence some of the ride price was covered by the refunded amount. The refunded orders are visible in the monthly rides.csv report (total ride price will show up as NULL). Unfortunately I don’t have access to BP to confirm how does it look like on client’s end for CC companies but in general I believe it should state there’s some extra amount on their balance there. Better to check with local ops or #business-support how does it show up on client’s end.

Clause 4.4: 
”4.4.          The Employee gives consent to the Employer to deduct any exceeded limits, for the services organized and ensured by the Employer (e.g. free ride) for the Employee, from the salary and other payments to be made to him/her during the employment period.”

Here the Employment contracts means the services requested by the Employee - of course the Employee is warned in advance about that and it’s made in line with Bolt’s policies, it’s not discretionary amount deducted without notice. For example, Bolt’s employees have a free credit of EUR 75 (or equivalent in other countries) for Bolt rides. If somehow the Employee actually spends EUR 80 for the rides, the 5 EUR will de deducted from the salary. 
Other example could be insurance for family members: (if agreed with the insurance company) Bolt may offer the Employee to add his spouse, kids, parents to the insurance and tell the cost in advance - if the Employee agrees, Bolt will pay for family members' insurance and then deduct its price from the Employee’s salary. 
Sometimes Bolt may offer courses (e.g. Estonian language) provided by third party schools for everyone interested and warn that the course is free if the Employee attends at least 70% of the lessons, but if he drops out without a valid reason and attend less then 30% of the classes, then he should compensate the company part of the amount paid for the course. 
To sup up, at each time the Employee is warned about the possible deduction and its amount. 

Clauses 3.8.14 and 9.3:
”While performing of job duties, the Employee is obliged:
To give preference to Company interests over personal interests and shall not enter into any relations or create grounds which will act as competition with the Company, as well as shall not cooperate with Company’s competitors in any matter as prescribed by the Agreement and shall strictly follow the terms and conditions of relevant agreement on non-competition and non-solicitation, and undertakes to immediately cease the violation of the obligation and additionally pay the Employer not less than the sum of average salary of the last 6 months (as the minimum amount of damage incurred by the Employer) for each instance of breach, by transferring this amount to the Employer's bank account within 10 (ten) calendar days as of receipt of a respective written claim. Such amount may be deducted from the Employee’s salary as per the applicable laws and full material liability agreement.” 
”The Parties have agreed that in case of violation of the obligation to keep the Business Secret the Employer is entitled to demand and the Employee undertakes to immediately cease the violation of the obligation and additionally pay the Employer not less than the sum of average salary of the last 6 months (as the minimum amount of damage incurred by the Employer) for each instance of breach, by transferring this amount to the Employer's bank account within 10 (ten) calendar days as of receipt of a respective written claim. The Employee is also required to compensate for damage, which exceeds the amount of contractual compensation. Such amount may be deducted from the Employee’s salary as per the applicable laws and full material liability agreement.”

These clauses say that should the Employee either cooperate with Bolt’s competitors or breach Confidentiality, he should pay the fine of 6 monthly salaries and this amount can be deducted from the payable salary. The amount of fine is pre-determined in the contract, but the Employer still needs to follow the employment law formalities and specify exactly what constituted breach - it can’t be vague or discretionary without reference to a particular event. If the Employee disagrees and believes that either he has not breached anything or the fine for the violation is excessive, the Employee can challenge this amount in court. Of course, the Employee can’t be deprived of his right to resort to court if he believes his rights have been breached - this stems from employment law. 
This process is similar to administrative fines - e.g. if someone’s car is parked in the area where parking is prohibited, the owner of the car receives a fine. But if he believes that something is incorrect and he hasn’t committed any violation, he can challenge the fine in court.

count (CASE WHEN payment_problem=1 THEN x.order_id END) AS count_pp,
CASE WHEN count_of_orders > 0 THEN ROUND(count_bad*1.0/count_of_orders,2) ELSE count_bad END AS count_ratio,
CASE WHEN sum_of_rides_eur > 0 THEN ROUND(sum_failed_payment_amount_eur*1.0/sum_of_rides_eur,2) ELSE sum_failed_payment_amount_eur END AS sum_ratio
FROM (
WITH destinations_distances AS (
SELECT 
cod.order_id,
cod.city_id,
distance_on_earth_km(co.real_destination_lat,co.real_destination_lng,cod.destination_lat,cod.destination_lng) AS distance_between_real_dest_and_entered_dest
FROM public.company_order co  
JOIN public.company_order_destination cod ON co.id = cod.order_id AND co.city_id = cod.city_id 
WHERE co.created >= '2022-04-01'
--AND cod.order_id = 902984445
--AND cod.city_id = 813
GROUP BY 1,2,co.real_destination_lat,co.real_destination_lng,cod.destination_lat,cod.destination_lng --2,3,4,5,6,7,8,co.real_destination_lat,co.real_destination_lng,ot.ride_price
),
min_distance AS (
SELECT 
cod.order_id AS order_id,
cod.city_id AS city_id,
CASE WHEN d.order_id IS NOT NULL THEN MIN (d.distance_between_real_dest_and_entered_dest) END AS min_distance
FROM company_order_destination cod
JOIN destinations_distances d ON cod.order_id = d.order_id AND cod.city_id = d.city_id
WHERE cod.created >= '2022-04-01'
--AND cod.order_id = 902984445
--AND cod.city_id = 813
GROUP BY 1,2,d.order_id
),
count_destinations AS (
SELECT city_id,
order_id,
COUNT(*) as count_of_destinations
FROM company_order_destination
WHERE created >= '2022-04-01'
--AND order_id = 902984445
--AND city_id = 813
GROUP BY 1,2
),
prediction AS (
SELECT p.order_id,
p.city_id,
p.distance,
p.predicted_price/r.rate AS predicted_eur
FROM pricing_order_prediction p 
JOIN company_order_try ot ON p.order_id = ot.order_id AND p.city_id = ot.city_id AND ot.state = 'finished'
LEFT JOIN public.currency_exchange_rates r ON DATE(r.valid_on) = DATE(p.created) AND r.currency = ot.price_currency 
WHERE p.created >= '2022-04-01'
--AND p.order_id = 903006868
--AND p.city_id = 386
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4
)
SELECT DISTINCT co.id AS order_id,
co.city_id AS city_id,
co.created AS created,
CONCAT (CONCAT (CONCAT ('https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/ride-hailing-order/orders/order/', co.id), '/' ),co.city_id) AS orderlink,
co.country,
ot.driver_id AS driver_id, 
ot.distance AS pickup_distance,
DATEDIFF('day',u.created, co.created) AS user_age,
md.min_distance AS min_distance,
cd.count_of_destinations,
ot.ride_price/r.rate AS ride_price_eur,
pred.predicted_eur,
ot.price/r.rate AS price_eur, 
COALESCE(tip.amount*1.0/r.rate,0) AS tip_eur,
pred.distance,
ot.ride_distance,
CASE 
	WHEN min_distance < 10 THEN '< than 10 kms' 
	WHEN min_distance BETWEEN 10 AND 20 THEN 'between 10 and 20 kms' 
	WHEN min_distance BETWEEN 20 AND 30 THEN 'between 20 and 30 kms' 
	WHEN min_distance BETWEEN 30 AND 40 THEN 'between 30 and 40 kms' 
	WHEN min_distance BETWEEN 40 AND 50 THEN 'between 40 and 50 kms' 
	WHEN 50 < min_distance THEN 'more than 50 kms' 
	END AS min_distance_in_ranges,
CASE WHEN o.last_payment_row_type='chargeback' THEN 'chargeback' WHEN o.payment_problem_state<>'ignored' THEN 'payment_problem' WHEN (o.last_payment_row_type='capture' AND o.last_payment_row_state='error') THEN 'failed_payment' ELSE o.last_payment_row_type||' '||o.last_payment_row_state END AS payment_type,
CASE WHEN payment_type = 'payment_problem' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS payment_problem, 
CASE WHEN payment_type = 'chargeback' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS chargeback,
CASE WHEN oa.id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS full_refund_order,
CASE WHEN (payment_type = 'failed_payment' AND o.uncovered_amount IS NULL) OR (o.uncovered_amount IS NOT NULL AND o.uncovered_amount != 0) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS failed_payment,
CASE WHEN (chargeback=1 OR failed_payment=1 OR payment_problem=1 OR full_refund_order=1) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS bad_payment,
ROUND(CASE WHEN (failed_payment = 1 AND o.uncovered_amount IS NULL) THEN o.capture_amount WHEN (o.booking_id IS NOT NULL AND o.uncovered_amount > 0) THEN o.uncovered_amount ELSE 0 END,2) AS failed_payment_amount,
ROUND(CASE WHEN (failed_payment = 1 AND o.uncovered_amount IS NULL) THEN o.capture_amount/r.rate WHEN (o.booking_id IS NOT NULL AND o.uncovered_amount > 0) THEN o.uncovered_amount/r.rate ELSE 0 END,2) AS failed_payment_amount_eur
FROM public.company_order co 
JOIN public.company_order_try ot ON co.id = ot.order_id AND co.city_id = ot.city_id AND ot.state = 'finished'
--JOIN destinations_distances d ON co.id = d.order_id AND co.city_id = d.city_id 
JOIN min_distance md ON md.order_id = co.id AND md.city_id = co.city_id 
LEFT JOIN count_destinations cd ON co.id = cd.order_id AND co.city_id = cd.city_id
--LEFT JOIN immutable_data_live.order_pricing_calculations opc ON opc.city_id = co.city_id AND opc.order_id = co.id 
LEFT JOIN commerce.orders o ON o.order_id = co.id AND o.city_id = co.city_id AND o.order_type = 'order'
LEFT JOIN public.currency_exchange_rates r ON DATE(r.valid_on) = DATE(co.created) AND r.currency = ot.price_currency 
LEFT JOIN public.ride_hailing_invoicing_order_pricing_transaction ptr ON ptr.order_id = co.id AND ptr.city_id = co.city_id 
LEFT JOIN public.ride_hailing_invoicing_tips_transaction_details tip ON tip.city_id = ptr.city_id AND tip.order_pricing_transaction_id = ptr.id 
LEFT JOIN pii.user_user u ON u.id = co.user_id 
LEFT JOIN public.fleet_driver fd ON fd.id = ot.driver_id 
LEFT JOIN public.fleet_driver_root fdr ON fdr.id = fd.driver_root_id
LEFT JOIN invoicing_refund_refund_log AS oa ON oa.order_id=o.id AND oa.city_id=o.city_id AND oa.state = 'done' AND oa.system_type = 'ride_hailing' AND oa.TYPE='full'
LEFT JOIN prediction pred ON co.id = pred.order_id AND co.city_id = pred.city_id
WHERE co.created >= '2022-04-01'
AND co.dispatcher_id IS NULL
AND co.reseller_id IS NULL
AND co.company_id IS NULL
AND co.payment_method_type NOT IN ('default','business')
--AND opc.hint <> 'bad_route_reestimate_distance'
--AND opc.hint <> 'bad_route'
AND cd.count_of_destinations = 1
--AND fdr.status <> 'blocked'
--AND bad_payment = 1 
--AND co.country = 'gb'
--AND ot.driver_id IN (1201709,1150402,989479,981479,2235712,1637792,1431711,1199714,1371114,1427490,1254371,464382,1087782,1299260,1260843,1047813,2523696,2220171,1277034)
--AND ride_price_eur > 100
AND ride_price_eur > 5*pred.predicted_eur 
AND price_eur > 20
AND user_age < 11
AND co.country NOT IN ('gb')
--AND md.min_distance > 5
--AND ot.driver_id = 2805219
--AND user_age < 1
--AND ot.distance < 50 
--AND co.id = 1125952196
--AND co.city_id = 55
--GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,o.last_payment_row_type,o.payment_problem_state,o.last_payment_row_state,o.uncovered_amount,o.booking_id,o.capture_amount,r.rate
) AS x
GROUP BY 1
--HAVING sum_failed_payment_amount_eur > 900
ORDER BY 5 DESC {code}

And this rejection was due to a different fraud rule: ‘DELIVERY_CASH_FRAUD’
[https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fraud/calculations/delivery_order_request/62048732|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fraud/calculations/delivery_order_request/62048732]

We have made a lot of amendments since February so we hope we’ve gotten more accurate with it now.

However, the initially reported account and your sister’s account both triggered the same rule “DELIVERY_ZA_FRAUD_REJECT”, we have 17 fraud patterns covered by the rule but they both triggered the same pattern as well.

I’ve looked into this further and found more false positives that we rejected. However, at the same time, this pattern stops a lot of fraudsters too. 

Both accounts had more than 5 trusted payments (means some time passed after the payment and there’s no risk of chargeback anymore), so I have implemented another condition into the pattern to exclude users with more than 5 trusted payments. This should prevent the rejection of eaters that have good history with us but coincidentally have similar information to the fraud pattern we saw.

Going forward if an unsuspected user triggers it, we should still proceed with verifying their account, but hopefully this will occur less now.

What we must keep in mind is that when a user opens the app, they will fall into 1 of 2 groups for whatever they need in that moment:

# I already know the service that I want, let me get it as quickly and easily as possible (i.e. I came to the app to rent a car, don’t bother me with scooters)
# I want to get to from point A to point B, and I’m willing to consider different methods of achieving that based on my wants and values

*What are the goals of the Mobility App?*

*First, the user statements:*

# As a new user, when I open the Bolt app, I want to quickly understand the services Bolt provides so I can select the one that suits my needs
# As an existing user, I want to be able to quickly access the service that I currently need
# As either a new or existing user, I want to have options for how to complete my trip. If I’m flexible on the mode of travel, I want to be able to optimize on cost or ETA
# As an existing user, I don’t want more steps/taps in order to use Bolt. I’ll tolerate change if I see the value, but don’t add more taps to my jobs to be done

*Stated from Bolt’s perspective:*

# We want to increase the number of trips per user. If a user is aware of all our services and can quickly access them, we should see more cross-pollination
# We want our users to get the most from our services. If they feel like the app is the right tool for their mobility needs, and they can optimize their usage based on their needs and values, they’ll be more likely to stick with us
# We want to be able to add new verticals without straining the IA or needing to reinvent the wheel
# We don’t want to create any additional hassle or effort for our existing user base, many of whom only use ride hailing, and will only ever use ride hailing, no matter what we do. We can’t alienate our core (and most profitable) users. So whatever we do, we should not increase effort (actual or perceived) to use ride hailing

MOV 12/ SOF 4 Smolensko store 

The goal of the experiment is to increase the Average Order Value without sacrificing the demand, and subsequently find a sweet spot where we can improve our profitability metrics per order.As you know, we don’t have proper mechanics that would allow us to A/B test the hypothesis, hence we are obliged to analyse the results retrospectively in comparison to other stores’ trends.

The preliminary results are quite promising and show no major change in conversion, while there is a steady increase in AOV and avg SOF (screenshot below). In parallel, we see a higher drop in the number of orders which we don’t account for the experiment because of the flat conversion rate _(default set-up: MOV - 10€, SOF - 3€; experiment set-up: MOV - 12€, SOF - 4€)._However, current data is not enough for us to make conclusive decisions; that’s why we decided to extend the experiment to all markets starting from next week, 25.07 . The proposal is to proceed with top-performing stores in capital cities which have minimum overlap. If there is an overlap — either choose top 2 or top 3 store or select multiple stores to improve the results of the experiment. [Here|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1oj08Ja_fNnfr__W16ILUlLHtUAPIHPqH-gCQp6ZKrrw/edit?usp=sharing] is the list of stores per market compiled by Edik.  Please review it and let me know if you have any objections or think we need to adjust it.

Hi [~accountid:621c92ba4160640069c52776] apologies for the delay, I was ooo until today. 

Not sure who signalled that there is an issue from a tax perspective - is it country specific? Overall, I don’t have an issue with either “Couriers get 100% of the tips” or “Bolt sends/gives 100% of the tips to couriers” from a tax perspective. Generally speaking:

* If the tip is paid to a freelance courier, they will normally be subject to a personal income tax on the tip amount in their country of residence regardless of the wording, i.e. it’s their additional income and they must declare it as part of their annual reporting. 
* If the tip is paid to a fleet as part of the overall service fee, the tip will likely be subject to a local corporation tax at the level of the fleet with the corresponding deduction where the tip is paid by the fleet to the relevant courier (who will then be subject to a personal income tax / employment taxes, as applicable, on the relevant amount).
* There should be no adverse VAT consequences on the basis that the tips paid by Eaters to couriers are voluntary (except for Croatia where tips are subject to VAT where the courier is VAT registered). 

There should be no adverse tax consequences for Bolt provided that Bolt will not retain any commission on the tips (which I understand is the case). As of 1 January 2023, Bolt will have to collect and report the information on the amount of tips (together with the rest of the payments) paid to each courier/fleet as part of the EU DAC7. If you have any questions relating to DAC7, please give me a shout.  

Hope this is clear but if you have any further question, please let me know. 

Thanks

Hi [~accountid:5b34a3b7c4ac74625bdc1020] , please find my comments below:

*A. Service Contract*

# +Clause 3.3. - Retention right:+ Schenker insists in having the right to withhold our goods and even sell them after 2 months in case of payment delays. I don’t think this is proportional and, since it’s a monetary risk for them (not being paid), it should be solved via a monetary mechanism, i.e., interest on delay which is already provided for in the agreement.
# +Clauses 4.2.5 and 4.2.6 - Schenker’s liability cap for lost goods:+ Schenker doesn’t seem to agree to deleting liability caps based on Special Drawing Rights (SDR). I suggest that we ask them how many SDR units would apply in each case, as there’s still only a placeholder for that. With that, we can evaluate whether their request is reasonable or not.
# +Clause 4.7 – Schenker’s liability cap for transportation services:+ Schenker insists in limiting their liability in this case to the lowest of the following: (i) in case of damage or loss, the value of goods per kilogram of the gross weight thereof or (ii) the remuneration for the specific service. This is too low in my opinion and, as previously mentioned, weight-based liability cap doesn’t make sense in our case since we’re mostly talking about Hardware.

*B. Customs Services Contract*

# +Clause 2.3 – Order refusal by Schenker:+ Schenker suggests that they communicate Bolt of any order refusal within 24h before commencing the services. The original timeline was 5h and we replaced it by 48h. Please let me know if 24h would be acceptable or if we should insist in 48h.
# +Clause 5.1 – Schenker’s liability cap regarding official fines:+ Schenker is not accepting to cap their liability in case of official fines caused by Schenker’s gross negligence or willful misconduct to the total value of the affected goods. They say it should be a percentage of average taxes and duties value per declaration. I don’t agree. In fact, their liability should be unlimited in this case in my opinion. We are already being flexible by accepting any liability cap at all.

*C. Others*

# Can you please confirm with Schenker that they are fine with all other changes they have not commented on?

Happy to have a quick alignment call if helpful.

Thanks and best,

Thiago

h3. *I want to report unknown charges*

Hi Romain,

thank you for raising this. I have reviewed the Ondato contract in the context of vendor’s liability for any privacy-related infringements.

The data processing terms included in the contract state that the limitations on liability set out in the main contract apply to all claims made pursuant to any privacy-related breach. And then in accordance with clause 12.2, the vendor might be liable only for the direct losses and the greatest amount payable them *may not exceed the amount payable for two months*, paid for respective services of the vendor.

This means that in case of any fine imposed on Bolt that would be caused by vendor’s processing practices, our recourse options may be significantly limited. Thus, using the services provided under this contract, may not be suitable for higher risk markets.

Kind regards,

Adriana

Hey Mateusz,

I checked the orders and found a fraud pattern, it seems like these are Ukraine fraudsters with ties with Belarus based on their info, and they were doing similar fraud in April in Poland and Ukraine too, just changed some details now.

I’ve written a new fraud rule PL_FRAUD_FOREIGN_CARDS_AND_IP which should stop them going forward. I’ll monitor the performance of the rule. You may sometimes see similar orders because this rule won’t be doing any rejects, instead we’ll give “CHALLENGE” response, triggering a 3DS verification to secure the payment and avoid chargebacks. Fraudsters should not pass this but sometimes banks don’t trigger the verification for their trusted users and just let the transaction through, in that case fraudster can still order but we won’t be losing any money as we asked for 3DSecure.

More info about the trips and analysis: [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1_lZwh9MUUJyf2iSCHA1fupppo0Qw1IS5iorGe5DwbuU/edit?usp=sharing|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1_lZwh9MUUJyf2iSCHA1fupppo0Qw1IS5iorGe5DwbuU/edit?usp=sharing|smart-link] 

Though the trips look prearranged it’s hard to prove driver involvement. I thought it was only new drivers at first but now I see that there is a lot of old driver accounts as well.  There’s no clear pattern between drivers and no repeating orders. As we’ll stop it from the user side now, the order will never happen so this should stop the driver fraud if there is any.

Please feel free to let me know if you have any questions.

Thanks\!

So, I’ve investigated following approaches:

* session-limited campaign, short lived enrolments.
With this we’ll be able to provide different discounts for user sessions, yet there might be some inconsistencies with session interruptions (i.e. user might see a discount, then app will be closed and for next (duration-of-enrolment) user won’t see anything).
Bad thing: there won’t be any possibility to limit number of discounts offered for user. One user might receive hundreds during duration of experiment.
Will require ~3-5d from lifecycle team
* session-limited campaign, session-limited enrolments
Same as above, yet there’ll be no interruptions.
Will require additional ~3-5d from platform team
* session-limited campaign, rolling enrolments (when targeting doesn’t care about previous enrolments, lets campaign decide what to do)
Same shortcomings as before, yet split of work will be slightly different:
lifecycle ~7d, platform ~3d
* session-limited bonus in campaign:
** new bonus, which will have something like {{percentages: [10, 20, 30, 40, 50]}} in configuration
** we enrol user once into that campaign
** whenever we need to decide on bonus value (before orders happens), we store in redis randomly selected bonus value from configuration (tied to session)
** This way we’ll have limited number of enrolments, we’ll have an ability to limit number of usages per user, we’ll avoid changes in targeting
** As this experiment is supposed to be for gathering data for ML for dynamic discount, we can think of using event buffer in order to publish data to redshift.
** Estimate would be ~7-10d from lifecycle for everything. Yet we’ll have a lot less disturbance for all other campaigns

The problem is it can take up to 10 business days before the charged amount is released by the user’s bank.
Explained here: [https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360005100694|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360005100694].

Sometimes this kind of complaint can be due to a delay in us charging a payment due to insufficient funds on the rider’s card.

*Short summary*: by agreement we may have the right to terminate the agreement with 2w advance notice, but we are bound to pay for the whole 12mo. 



*Longer explanation:* 



+Notification of termination+ 

From the task description I cannot see that any of the preconditions for immediate termination have been met (cl 7 second para). 

The agreement foresees that the upon the completion of the pilot period, both parties could at that specific point in time terminate the Agreement by giving two weeks written notice. The agreement does not specify how long is “the pilot period”. Nevertheless, It is unreasonable to assume, that pilot period would last for the whole term of the Agreement. 

By definition “the pilot period” means a period of time during which the service is tested. It is an initial small-scale implementation that is used to prove the viability of the service. The pilot project enables an organisation to manage the risk of a new idea and identify any deficiencies before substantial resources are committed.

Thus, in accordance with the spirit of the contract and applicable law (Dutch), the “the pilot period” cannot be considered the whole term of the Agreement, but (as described by you) it was a period up to 3 months i the beginning of the term. Consequently, as this pilot period has now over, then both parties have the right at any specific point in time terminate the Agreement by giving two weeks written notice. 



+Payments+

Now, the next paragraph of the Agreement states that “Upon termination of this Agreement (for any reason), any and all unpaid and properly due amounts and any accrued obligations shall survive the termination of this Agreement.”  

Clause 2 of the Agreement states, that “This contract is set for a period of 12 months. This contract will start on the 10^th^ of January 2022 and will be terminated on the 10^th^ of January 2023. The price per month for the 12 month period is stated below and represents the monthly cost for the period per resource.”

In combinations, these two paragraphs clearly and unambiguously state that even in the case of early termination, the customer will have an obligation to pay for all 12mo. 





Regards

Marja-Liisa

Hey again [~accountid:619628e6b0b630006a6d2919],

In case of notice 1 in [the process|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3935895630/Delivery+Provider+fraud+escalation+flow], we do not payout any balance.

Though in other scenarios, we do not have a solid proof that would connect the provider to the fraud scheme. This is mainly because of technical limitations - they use designated tablets which are not for personal use, and those have completely different details than the fraudulent orders - so we don’t have much data to connect them to fraud, except for fraudulent payment rates that we get to know of with chargebacks and fraud notifications from banks. 

When that’s the case, the provider can dispute the offboarding and payout holds, can demand a payment or explanation, also can claim that they were attacked by fraudsters and they’re not related. As we can’t prove anything, it can put us in a difficult situation and create lots of work with legal team. Notice 2 gives us the possibility to offboard a provider with 30 day notice without having to provide any reason, but for payouts we still have to rely on solid evidence while paying out to them.

In order to prevent them from making more possibly fraudulent money, we use the blacklist feature to do 3DSecure on orders with new cards. As Ukraine doesn’t have 3DS available right now, such orders will be rejected right away for the time being. 

Hopefully when 3D Secure is implemented in the following quarter, we will be able to put on way more extensive fraud rules which won’t hurt good users and reduce such issues. Let me know if you have more questions 🙏 

Thanks

I have opened this Legal Ticket to recap on a couple of different slack discussions + to centralize the current advice + agree on the next steps.



+*Document for basis of discussion*+: Bolt Club Guidelines [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1X3FsFL8-tbpVFrGr8weoFvlavHkw1YEmtp6TDOZgLaQ/edit#heading=h.m3qcg19usw0i|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1X3FsFL8-tbpVFrGr8weoFvlavHkw1YEmtp6TDOZgLaQ/edit#heading=h.m3qcg19usw0i|smart-link] 

+*Important ‘legal’ points from the Guidelines*+ (recommendations from [~accountid:5fa118a781b2880078eb0e6f] as Product Counsel for RH and Privacy Team)*:*

* It is not possible at this stage to *modulate the rewards / show different discounts based on drivers' performance metrics* → The same rewards should be offered to all drivers (this might change in the future, depending on the outcome of discussions within Legal).
* *It is not possible at this stage to subsidize any offers* → Any financial commitment by Bolt to underwrite discounts offered by Partner (e.g. by contributing equity or make financial guarantees) exposes Bolt to enhanced reclassification risk (as an argument could be made that essentially Bolt is providing/financing provision of essential tools to deliver transport services).
* As a rule, personal data of Drivers should not be shared with the Partner. If sharing personal data with the Partner is necessary, *personal data may be shared under legitimate interest legal basis.* Our template Partnership Agreement states that the parties remain separate data controllers and a *Data Sharing Agreement* needs to be completed and signed. Key principles are:  *necessity + data minimisation* (only share personal data which is strictly necessary for the agreed purposes & any additional data sharing shall be conducted in anonymised format).



In order to run some comparison with what our competitors do, I did some +*research into the Uber loyalty program*+ - which is public (at least its main features): [https://www.uber.com/fr/fr/drive/uber-pro/|https://www.uber.com/fr/fr/drive/uber-pro/] . Here are the main points how I understand them:

* Uber publicly explains very clearly how you can benefit from the *Gold, Platinum or Diamond statuts*.
* *They takes into account 1. the note given by riders, 2. the cancellation rate and 3. the number of rides.*
* All these metrics seem to be calculated over a period of 3 months and then every 3 months you start again at 0.
* Each status gives the drivers access to various benefits (as detailed on their page).

*What I think:*

* I'm surprised that Uber looks at cancellation rates + notes - I think that looking just at the number of rides might be more objective/safer.
* I'm very *surprised by some benefits*, such as (in terms of most surprising benefits from my perspective): 1. Priority given to drivers's messages and calls, 2. Increased priority for airports, 3. Interest-free loans and 4. Additional destination (BTW apparently they have a daily limit?) - and apparently statuts are publicly available to riders.
* This Uber loyalty program seems quite risky from a legal perspective - however question whether *we could be more relaxed about creating tiers/statuts, perhaps just based on the number of rides performed*. If we just do that without subsidizing any offers, perhaps it would not increase that much the reclassification risks. I understand the FR team also hopes to *subsidizes offers* (either by paying the partners or the drivers), to be able to have really attractive offers --> Would that really increase the reclassifications risks, or would that be quite similar to offering 'guaranteed prices' for any 3 rides within X hours or subsidizing trainings to become a VTC driver - TBD.
* I wonder if Uber’s *reinitialization of its program every 3 months* is to reduce any reclassification risks?



+*Some feedback from*+ [~accountid:5fa118a781b2880078eb0e6f] +*/ the Legal team*+ (Thanks a lot [~accountid:5fa118a781b2880078eb0e6f] for your inout so far):

*Starting facts about Bolt Club:*

* *Product feature does not currently support the ability to show different offers to different drivers based on performance* - this is a plan for the future.
* More complex partnership deal structures (with investment, subsidy, commitment) can still happen. But HQ teams (BussDev / C.Ops) should be involved and will be cleared on case-by-case basis.
* Legally we are in general *concerned about additional re-class risk brought by both 1. subsidizing essential tools and 2. making offers based on performance*. BUT this only signals that more thinking and scrutiny needs to go into this. As per guidelines:
** Additional risk from *subsidizing*, as a prudent precaution, should be assessed separately for each market before implementing -> {color:#4c9aff}*so in FR we could check if under current re-class case-law the fact that Bolt partially pays for essential tools (like fuel, like car maintenance) is a marker of employment*{color}. NB/ for other countries (eg PT) we could check whether the market supply set-up (e.g. supply through fleets employing drivers) could mitigate the risks.
** *Performance based offer*: legal framework for this has not yet been constructed as it is for the Bolt Club MVP stage - is outside the scope. But here are some early thoughts to be further discussed:
*** Subsidizing fuel for drivers based on performance - looks problematic.
*** However, could we envisage shaping this the same way as a standard “campaign offer” - where we offer economic incentive (in shape of non-cash benefit) for driver service delivers (so completed rides, instead of “performance” while logged-in aka Acceptance Rates).

*General thoughts on Uber Gold/Platinum/Diamond program*:

* This goes into prioritization based on performance; and seems more relevant in our thinking about prioritized despatch based on Driver Score, Finished Rides, engagement metric etc.
* {color:#bf2600}*It was scrutinized in NL by courts in a reclassification case*{color} and the courts said: yes loyalty program based prioritization/benefits may not look like controlling access to work and more like incentives (which is ok’ish) but the fact that Uber solely controls these benefits and can take them away at any time - *is a marker of employment*. Appeal in the case will be heard in early 2023. (thanks [~accountid:5fa118a781b2880078eb0e6f] for bringing this to my attention).

*General thinking about incentives:* 

* It seems much better than blocks
* They should be ideally purely financial in nature
* They could perhaps be OK if it incentivizes the final result and objective service quality instead of “performance on the job” (so finished rides, instead of acceptance/cancelation rates)

*Passive data collecting works in the background and active data collecting works only when users are actively using our app. So the best case scenario for us would be if data is collected passively, I hope that clarifies the question above.*



This is quite complex project privacy-wise, and I’d appreciate if you could please provide additional context here, but general legal requirements for localisation-based marketing are as follows:

*A little context:*  
*Rentals have taken great initiative in order to increase usage of our scooters in all of our respective cities but with limited marketing budget and very rigid permits, I thought of a new way that may help us solve this problem. Which is geofencing. So if a customer is for example at a bus stop and we have this specific bus stop geofenced, I would like to have the option of sending this customer a push notification saying something like ‘hey heading home? Why not take one of our scooters located at X” or “hey heading into the city why not unlock our scooter for just 1kr/min” in order to generate more rides and in turn more GMV.*



collecting any information about a user's location when the app is closed would constitute very high privacy risk; under GDPR using localisation for marketing purposes would require consent. You can utilise existing consent modules in Bolt App for this purposes;

in Bolt privacy policy we state that Bolt only uses user’s localisation for service-related purposes, so if you’d like to proceed with this project both SE and DK privacy policies would need to be updated;

*How often are the privacy policies updated? In this case would it be possible to amend the wording so we can collect the data we need? What would be the implications?*

under article 35 of GDPR, processing activities that involve processing data at large scale should be subject to documented data protection impact assessment which is a type of formal and documented privacy analysis. While this requirement won’t materialise for the proof-of-concept stage, if this project will be considered to be rolled out on broader scale, then appropriate assessment would be mandatory (this page is still in work-in-progress but provides some overview on the process);

and finally, as with all push notifications, those would also require end user granting appropriate permissions on their device to receive such communication.

*In regards to the push notification feature, aren’t there other verticals in the business that use this feature already such as ride hailing or bolt food when sending out promotions etc? Are the privacy policies different depending on the vertical?*

Hi there Samuel.

First of all, did you follow the procedure from the CS training related to fraud price reviews and discussed this case with your TL and with OPS before creating this escalation?

!PR workflow.png|width=50%!

About the ride itself, I think you misunderstood the decision that was made from our side. We didn’t refund this ride because we thought they were done without the passenger inside the car. From the route points visible in the system, we know the driver did the kilometers. That’s not the point. We’ve refunded because this ride wasn’t logged/approved in the App. The ride request had a really low prediction and there’s no destination change logged/approved in the App to justify the route the driver made. If the payment were successful, refund wouldn’t happen from our side. So even if the ride was empty, if we collected the money, would stay like that until the customer complained and CS would do a usual refund.

Please be careful with your interpretation. This ride is fraudulent. The payment method is intentionally a bad one that returned an insufficient funds payment error. Please don’t compensate the driver this amount back.

We are covered by the [TOS|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/rs/terms-for-drivers/]:
{{6.5. We are not obliged to pay you the Fare due from the Passenger if the In-app Payment failed because Passenger's credit card or other payment is cancelled or is unsuccessful for other reasons.}}

Drivers have to be educated that if the passenger requests a new destination, they have to log that in the App and wait for approval. If we don’t approve the change, they have to follow the message that is displayed to them in the App (screenshot)

!Screenshot 2022-07-18 at 13.29.27.png|width=50%!

So for these cases with low predictions and no destination change, we’ll always try to collect the money. But if the payment fails, we’ll refund it and drivers shouldn’t be compensated when we make this decision to refund.

We need to add a default value for the field {{taxify_reseller.order_report.start_date}} and/or {{taxify_reseller.order_report.end_date}}


The DB servers has the {{explicit_defaults_for_timestamp}} disabled. This means that {{TIMESTAMP}} columns following the first one, must: *Explicitly allow* {{NULL}} *or have a* {{DEFAULT}} *value.* Otherwise the automatic {{DEFAULT}} is {{'0000-00-00 00:00:00'}}

{noformat}mysql> SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'explicit_defaults_for_timestamp';
+---------------------------------+-------+
| Variable_name                   | Value |
+---------------------------------+-------+
| explicit_defaults_for_timestamp | OFF   |
+---------------------------------+-------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec){noformat}

 

The field {{end_date}}:

* Is not the first {{TIMESTAMP}} type,
* It is declared as {{NOT NULL}}
* and it has no explicit {{DEFAULT}}

So MySQL automatically declared as {{DEFAULT '0000-00-00 00:00:00'}}.

_Please refer to_ [MySQL 5.7 Reference Manual :: sysvar_explicit_defaults_for_timestamp|https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.7/en/server-system-variables.html#sysvar_explicit_defaults_for_timestamp]

 

With this, we hit another restriction:

The {{sql_mode}} in DB servers has includes {{NO_ZERO_DATE}}, which means that the {{DEFAULT '0000-00-00 00:00:00'}} is not a valid value.

{noformat}mysql> SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'sql_mode';
+---------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Variable_name | Value                                                                                                                              |
+---------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| sql_mode      | IGNORE_SPACE,ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY,STRICT_TRANS_TABLES,NO_ZERO_IN_DATE,NO_ZERO_DATE,ERROR_FOR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO,NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION |
+---------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
1 row in set (0.01 sec){noformat}

_Please refer to_ [MySQL 5.7 Reference Manual :: SQL Mode :: NO_ZERO_DATE|https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.7/en/sql-mode.html#sqlmode_no_zero_date]

 

An attempt to create the table as described above will fail with the following error: {{ERROR 1067 (42000): Invalid default value for 'end_date'}}

 

Possible solutions are:

# Enable {{explicit_defaults_for_timestamp}}, which requires further analysis, as the database servers are shared hosts and the change will apply to other services.
# Explicitly declare a default non zero value i.e. {{due_time TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP}}.
# Explicitly declared with the {{NULL}} attribute.

There are 2 different steps: (1) the +approval of annual accounts+ by the shareholder(s), and (2) the +filing of the approved accounts+ with the local registry.

However, we strongly recommend that Bolt France’s annual accounts be approved by its sole shareholder.

Please note that, to be compliant while keeping their accounts confidential, small and medium-sized companies (_petites entreprises et micro-entreprises)_, may file a total or partial declaration of confidentiality of their financial statements depending on the category of the company.

We also draw your attention to the fact that, at the end of each financial year, it is required to check whether it is mandatory or not for the company to appoint a Statutory Auditor if it has reached the legal thresholds (the number of employees, balance sheet value and turnover).

+*Advice received from external counsel (OC, Tonya Aelbrecht), 12 July:*+

We are following up on your question with regard to the replacement of Anneli Aljas as a director in Bolt Support Services BE SRL (the "*Company*").

It is indeed possible to have only one director in the Company. There is therefore no requirement to replace Anneli Aljas as a director, and consequently Ahto Kink may remain the sole director of the Company.

# Procedure

Under Belgian law, Ms Aljas can resign as a director of the Company by mere notification to the Company. In practice, we recommend having the resigning director sign a resignation letter, in which Ms Aljas resigns as a director of the Company (with immediate effect or with effect from a particular date) and requests for her resignation to be published as soon as possible in accordance with applicable law. Her resignation would then be acknowledged by the remaining director of the Company (or, if a new director is appointed to replace Ms Aljas, in resolutions of the shareholders of the Company in which the new director is also appointed).

Alternatively, if Ms Aljas is no longer available to sign a resignation letter, the shareholders' meeting may at any time decide to terminate the mandate of Ms Aljas (with immediate effect or with effect from a particular date). This requires resolutions of the sole shareholder of the Company.

Upon your request we would be happy to prepare (i) a resignation letter and resolutions of the sole director or (ii) written resolutions of the sole shareholder.

# Publication formalities

Moreover, in order to render the termination of Ms Aljas' mandate opposable to third parties, the resignation or decision of the sole shareholder to terminate her mandate must be published in the annexes to the Belgian State Gazette. We typically include a PoA to us (OC) in the relevant resolutions to take care of the publication formalities.

# Fee quote

For the above work, our fees would typically amount to EUR *1,000* (excl. VAT and disbursements).

* In order to address a fine to the responsible person, the police need to send a form with the following details - if they’re not provided, they won’t accept the form (they refuse to look for addresses themselves as it is time-consuming):
** Full name
** ID code or birth date
** DL number
** Address
*  The police doesn’t care if the address is fake or if the user lives there or not, they need to send the fine in an envelope. Once they receive an address from us and it suits their requirements - we are no longer responsible for paying the fine.

* Richard Chahine confirmed that in Sweden, the social security number is required but not the address as they will use the tax registered address for that person. The user would have to approve with BankiD to check their driving licence.
* Currently, OPS request CS to contact users who don’t have an address or a valid one provided for their user account (although providing the address is required by our T&C). With outbound calls not being available in Beehive, the only options are:
** For OPS to call users from their phone number (which may be sketchy - some unknown person calling the user asking for their address)
** Block the user to make them contact us (not very user-friendly)

Hi [~accountid:627e2cd90e2c49006904d45e] Please find below my feedback on this request + the templates I have created for you 😉 

* +*Key principles:*+
** If we’re looking into *paying for using someone’s image*, then no GDPR-related wording will be required in the agreement itself, as the processing will be carried out on the basis of *contractual necessity*.
** Otherwise, for *non-paid partnerships*, as someone’s image is classified as personal data, the processing is usually based on *data subject’s consent* which unfortunately means that it can be revoked at any time. 

→ So bottom line, if we don't pay the person and we say it's a consent to use her image rights for X years, this may be not enforceable as under GDPR the consent can be withdrawn at any time.

→ If we want to secure the right to use someone’s image rights for X years, we need to include some benefit that can be provided by Bolt to make it more of a contract. Then we can process their image based on contractual necessity and the data subject won’t be able to withdraw their consent.

_Note:_ Giving that person Bolt vouchers of EUR 100 should be fine, it seems substantial enough to consider that a payment. It would give us a leeway to argue that the usage of the image is then carried out based on contractual necessity and not on data subject’s consent. 

_However_ if the cost of production if very substantial and we don’t want to take any risk of a dispute, then a more structured approach with a formalized agreement and a more substantial payment would be preferable.

* +*Legal documents / templates:*+
** *For non paid partnership (and revocable right to use image)*: You need to ask the person to sign a +Consentement d’exploitation de droit à l’image+: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1cNKG16SHrKZQbX_kZTOSmRcUglP2fAwG/edit|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1cNKG16SHrKZQbX_kZTOSmRcUglP2fAwG/edit|smart-link] (Please always save it as a new document, as this is a template).
** *For a non-revocable, fixed term right o use images, including financial compensation*: You need to ask the person to sign an +Autorisation d’exploitation de droit à l’image+: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1HQg4_QtfTgBexjLF5KKVkBaLDhjjVoXb/edit|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1HQg4_QtfTgBexjLF5KKVkBaLDhjjVoXb/edit|smart-link] (Please always save it as a new document, as this is a template).
** *Each of the above document should be accompanied by a Privacy notice* - this document +should be provided+ (no need to sign) to each data subject and should accompany the Consent/Authorization. Please review the document to make sure it covers all of your expected use cases and add the information on possible data recipients. [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1567IcspFYXIq4kv_0jaCN-QD4qa_1CrE/edit#heading=h.p80iefflg1fb|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1567IcspFYXIq4kv_0jaCN-QD4qa_1CrE/edit#heading=h.p80iefflg1fb|smart-link]
* 
* +*Important remarks from the IP Team:*+
** *make sure not to include any copyrighted content* - such as songs we don’t have a right to use (even if e.g. that would be only sung by the driver/rider);
** *pay attention to the logos that may appear on the recording* (e.g. logos on riders' clothing) - those should be blurred.

Once a document has had the legal review and has been approved for signing by the relevant legal counsel - our legal operations team will arrange the signature based on the request e.g. electronic signing via Hellosign or a wet ink original and they will clarify who is signing i.e. HQ (Ahto Kink usually) or somebody else under a PoA (and this is why having singing details at the outset is key to ensuring this process is as smooth as possible).

 Assuming we have all the details (e.g. name and email address if dealing with Hellosign) this step is usually done within the same day (however sometimes there is a backlog or holiday absence meaning it can take a day or two; or if a notary signature is required then this can take a few working days).  We of course cannot control how quickly the counterparty will sign using Hellosign (but can send them reminders). Once both parties have signed (using Hellosign) then the document is complete and a copy is uploaded to the ticket. 

If signature was organised via HQ - then legal ops will arrange for the contract to be archived. If the signature step was arranged by the business - then please provide the scan to [contracts@bolt.eu|mailto:contracts@bolt.eu] and ensure the original (if signed using wet ink) is kept in a safe place or provided to legal HQ for safekeeping.

Part of the risk and safety team had a meeting with the Ukrainian team last week and this is what was reported back:

** No trip but online → go to a safe place

* About payment, here it’s also mainly an ops decision. This is how I would do it, but you should agree with your local team. 
** Card payment → complete in the app, in case of issues, the passenger can contact CS
** Cash payment:

*** Underpay → driver can contact CS (I would not block passengers, compensation decisions are up to the ops team).

Thanks and let me know if you have more questions.

Hi,

Q1: There is no such time limit in mentioned legislation. Of course, there are some limitations – among others, Bolt is obliged to maintain at the workplace a quantity of fire-hazardous materials which is +*no greater than the daily demand or daily production*+ (Polish: _dobowe zapotrzebowanie lub dobowa produkcja_). The excess shall be stored in separate warehouse adjusted to this purpose. So, it does not strictly mean that the batteries can be kept on-site for 24 hours only, the regulation applies to the quantity of hazardous materials stored, not timing.

Please keep in mind that according to this legislation (§ 7), any activities related to fire-hazardous material shall be exercised in accordance with fire-safety instruction covering the site (§ 6) and with conditions specified by the manufacturer of the batteries. Thus, if such 24-hour limitation is indicated in the instruction or on the conditions, then it is binding.

Q2: Irrespective of the fact that storage of hazardous materials may violate the provisions of some lease agreements, in case of fire caused by inflammation of scooter stored without necessary safety measures you may be declined any insurance amounts. However, this may have even more dangerous consequences called “construction disaster” (event that threatens the life or health of many people or property in large sizes, in the form, f.eg. of fire collapse of structures), is punishable by imprisonment from one year to 10 years (in cause of unintentional disaster is punishable by imprisonment from 3 months to 5 years). Irrespective of the above, the building incompliant with fire protection requirements may be subject to compulsory closure.

*PL*:

Art. 163 ustawy z dnia 6 czerwca 1997 r. Kodeks Karny

§ 1. Kto sprowadza zdarzenie, które zagraża życiu lub zdrowiu wielu osób albo mieniu w wielkich rozmiarach, mające postać:

# pożaru,

# zawalenia się budowli, zalewu albo obsunięcia się ziemi, skał lub śniegu,

# eksplozji materiałów wybuchowych lub łatwopalnych albo innego gwałtownego wyzwolenia energii, rozprzestrzeniania się substancji trujących, duszących lub parzących,

# gwałtownego wyzwolenia energii jądrowej lub wyzwolenia promieniowania jonizującego, podlega karze pozbawienia wolności od roku do lat 10.

§ 2. Jeżeli sprawca działa nieumyślnie, podlega karze pozbawienia wolności od 3 miesięcy do lat 5.

§ 3. Jeżeli następstwem czynu określonego w § 1 jest śmierć człowieka lub ciężki uszczerbek na zdrowiu wielu osób, sprawca podlega karze pozbawienia wolności od lat 2 do 12.

§ 4. Jeżeli następstwem czynu określonego w § 2 jest śmierć człowieka lub ciężki uszczerbek na zdrowiu wielu osób, sprawca podlega karze pozbawienia wolności od 6 miesięcy do lat 8.

 

*ENG:*

Art.  163. of Criminal Code of June 6, 1997

§ 1. Whoever brings about an incident threatening life and health of multiple persons or property of great extent, in the form of:

# a fire,

# a collapse of a structure, flooding, or landslide, rockslide or snowslide,

# an explosion of explosive or flammable materials, or other violent release of energy, spreading of poisonous, asphyxiating or blistering substances,

# a violent release of nuclear energy or ionising radiation,

is subject to the penalty of deprivation of liberty for between one year and 10 years.

§ 2. If the perpetrator acts unintentionally, he is subject to the penalty of deprivation of liberty for between 3 months and 5 years.

§ 3. If the consequence of the act referred to in § 1 is the death of a human or a grievous bodily harm to multiple persons, the perpetrator is subject to the penalty of deprivation of liberty for between 2 years and 12 years.

§ 4. If the consequence of the act referred to in § 2 is the death of a human or a grievous bodily harm to multiple persons, the perpetrator is subject to the penalty of deprivation of liberty for between 6 months and 8 years.

It seems all the problem here was because we had fallbacks for the start and finish times.

To achieve what we want we have to get these values only from the order type, if it is not there it will be null. 

Here is the part of the query that is get the state and finish time correctly. Notice that it does not have any relation with the Order State, once what defines the times where the driver started driving with the client and the time where the driver arrived to the destination is the order try.

{color:#ff5630}It is still open how the order try states behave with multiple stops{color}

{noformat}.....
UNIX_TIMESTAMP(sls.created) AS start_time,
UNIX_TIMESTAMP(sle.created) AS finish_time,
.....
LEFT JOIN
  ${TableId.orderTryStateLog} as sls ON (sls.order_try_id = ot.id AND sls.to_state = ${OrderTryState.DRIVING_WITH_CLIENT})
LEFT JOIN
  ${TableId.orderTryStateLog} AS sle ON (sle.order_try_id = ot.id AND sle.to_state = ${OrderTryState.ARRIVED_TO_DESTINATION})
.....{noformat}

# *What are general principles for temporary work, i.e., for how long term, how many consecutive terms within what period; any additional need to justify the temporary agreement, etc?*

Temporary work is based on three vertices: the client, Bolt, the temporary work company, Triangulu, and the worker. There are two contracts: the contract that the client has with the temporary work company, with the payment conditions and the assignment of the temporary agency employee to the client, and the contract between the temporary work company and the worker, in which Bolt has no intervention.
There must be a justification for using temporary work, and depending on the justification, the maximum duration of this type of contract can range from 6 months to 2 years. The justifications may be increased workload, seasonal activity, intermittent need for labor, direct replacement of an employee on leave without pay, etc.
The contract for the use of temporary work is always for a maximum of 2 years, BUT it can be renewed with new justification - hypothetically, if there is an increased need for labor in a seasonal activity, a new contract can be made.

*2. Are the workers brought in under this service provider’s agreement considered service provider’s or Bolt’s employees?*

The workers are temporary agency workers, not Bolt workers. They are “loaned” by the the company to Bolt to perform the agreed services. However, since they are “on loan” there are some responsibilities that Bolt has, such as training, ensuring working conditions, evaluation, as well as monthly passing on the information of actual hours worked so that the temp company can process workers’ salary. At the end of the month, a receipt is sent for payment from the company to Bolt, just like any other service rendered.

*3. What are the main risks with this service provider’s agreement (e.g on could initial fixed-term contracts be considered open-ended etc)?*

Right now, the contracts that Bolt has with Triangulu are contracts for an uncertain term, since the justification that was used allows us to have up to two years, and when there is no longer a need we can terminate the contract. Which means, that they cannot be open-ended. After 2 years, we need to set up a new one. The main risk is to ensure that the contracts do not exceed this period (10 days after the non-existence of a contract the worker is considered a Bolt worker).

This type of service is in terms of cost cheaper than outsourcing, because part of what is outsourced is done internally by Bolt - all the training, working conditions,  daily management, vacations, and others. At the same time, there is a much more efficient control over productivity and results, so it ends up being a balance that makes more sense for some verticals. Also, Bolt is involved directly in recruiting people (hiring managers interview candidates, so a sort of external hiring agency).

The biggest risk, however, is the legislation on temporary work is being discussed in parliament this year - there is talk of limiting the conditions and justifications why there are many companies that avoid hiring internally to do it this way.

{code:sql}SELECT x.driver_id,
x.week_diff_til_now,
SUM(x.order_marked) AS count_marked,
count (DISTINCT x.order_id) AS count_orders,
CASE WHEN count_orders > 0 THEN count_marked*1.0/count_orders END AS ratio,
SUM(CASE WHEN x.order_marked = 1 THEN x.price_eur END) AS sum_fraud_eur,
avg(x.fraud_score) AS avg_fraud_score,
COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN x.in_app = 1 THEN x.order_id END) AS count_in_app,
CASE WHEN count_orders > 0 THEN count_in_app*1.0/count_orders END AS ratio_in_app,
avg(x.user_age) AS avg_user_age
FROM ( 
SELECT DISTINCT co.created, 
CASE
    WHEN DATE_PART(w, CURRENT_DATE) - DATE_PART(w, co.created) < 0 THEN DATE_PART(w, CURRENT_DATE) - DATE_PART(w, co.created) + 52
    WHEN DATE_PART(w, CURRENT_DATE) - DATE_PART(w, co.created) >= 0 THEN DATE_PART(w, CURRENT_DATE) - DATE_PART(w, co.created)
END AS week_diff_til_now,
co.id AS order_id,
co.city_id, 
ot.driver_id,
CASE WHEN oa.id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS order_marked,
ot.price/r.rate AS price_eur,
co.fraud_score,
CASE WHEN co.payment_method_type NOT IN ('default','business') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS in_app,

LEFT JOIN fraud_action_order_action oa ON oa.order_id = co.id AND oa.city_id = co.city_id 
LEFT JOIN vw_currency_exchange_rates as r ON r.currency=ot.price_currency AND DATE(r.valid_on)=DATE(co.created)

GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,co.payment_method_type,10
) AS x

HAVING ratio_in_app >= 0.8
AND avg_fraud_score >= 0

Hey all\!


*1.Do I understand correctly, that we have signed a* [*temporary agency work*|https://eur-lex.europa.eu/LexUriServ/LexUriServ.do?uri=OJ:L:2008:327:0009:0014:EN:PDF] *agreement where:*

* *Triangulu is temporary-work agency;*
* *Bolt is user undertaking, and*
* *the worker in question is temporary agency worker (a worker with a contract of employment or an employment relationship with a temporary-work agency with a view to being assigned to a user undertaking to work temporarily under its supervision and direction)?*

Precisely. However, the contracts we set up are mostly focused on specific positions or specific needs. For instance, we have 5 specific back-office agents for Ride-Hailing - the contract only covers this specific profile; if  Rentals is hiring mechanics through the temp agency, as the role is different, so are the fees/justification for the use of temp work, so a new contract is required. There is also no exclusivity with Triangulu as a temp-work agency.

*2. Who actually keeps track whether the worker is working temporarily for a fixed term to avoid any possible reclassification from temporary agency worker to direct employee of Bolt?*  

That would be me + the direct managers of said workers due to a more hands-on management, at the moment. As we currently only have 10 temp workers (5 mechanics + 5 back-office agents), using the same agency, tracking it is fairly easy. However, a potential increase in the number of temp workers will need to have a readjustment of the process and all required steps in the communication with the temp agency: for instance, these workers are setup in WD as regular contractors, no contract end date, and that can be something to work on going forward.

Just to give a bit more details regarding the usage of temp work, legally we need to give the same salary conditions to someone internal with the same role - it has been working well thus far mostly because we don’t have any internal employees in the same roles as these workers. If we are to use temporary work to hire, say, Customer Support Specialists, we’d be legally obliged to make sure that they have the same salary conditions as our internal CSS.

I’ve set up a quick table with main operational differences between Temporary Work and Outsourcing, feel free to check it [here|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1YWwxqQFlF3a-8bmjFjzw5oFL8eHzOxAZZzUbZXLTffQ/edit?usp=sharing].

Hey\! Adding here advice I received some time ago from external counsel. Hope it will be helpful.

_“The requirements for selling medicines differ depending on their type:_

 _Retail sales of_ *_prescription and non-prescription medicines_* _requires a_ +_pharmacy license_+_, which can be obtained in accordance with the Cabinet of Ministers Regulation No 800_ [_“Procedures for the Licensing of Pharmaceutical Activity”_|https://likumi.lv/ta/en/en/id/238458-procedures-for-the-licensing-of-pharmaceutical-activity]_._

 _Such a license requires registration with the State Agency of Medicines and a physical pharmacy to be established which conforms to the requirements of the_ [_Pharmaceutical Law_|https://likumi.lv/ta/en/en/id/43127]_, Cabinet of Ministers Regulation No 288_ [_“Regulations Regarding Operating of Pharmacies”_|https://likumi.lv/ta/en/en/id/207397-regulations-regarding-operating-of-pharmacies]_, Cabinet of Ministers Regulation No 610_ [_“Criteria for the Location of Pharmacies and Pharmacy Branches”_|https://likumi.lv/ta/en/en/id/234279-criteria-for-the-location-of-pharmacies-and-pharmacy-branches] _and the aforementioned Cabinet of Ministers Regulation No 800_ [_“Procedures for the Licensing of Pharmaceutical Activity”_|https://likumi.lv/ta/en/en/id/238458-procedures-for-the-licensing-of-pharmaceutical-activity]_._

 _Furthermore, only_ *_non-prescription medicine_* _can be sold remotely (through a distance sale) and the pharmacy license must contain a special condition allowing such. The requirements for obtaining a special condition are:_

* _the possibility for the buyers to communicate with the pharmacy via the website during working hours and to receive free of charge information and consultations from the abovementioned medicinal products in the provision of pharmaceutical care in accordance with the laws and regulations regarding the requirements for the opening and operation of the pharmacy;_
* _a website that is established in accordance with the_ [_Law On Information Society Services_|https://likumi.lv/ta/en/en/id/96619-law-on-information-society-services]_, which is accessible to the buyer at any hour of the day without interruption, and the information posted therein conforms to the laws and regulations regarding advertising of medicinal products;_
* _notification to the Health Inspectorate and the State Agency of Medicines of the date when the remote sales will begin, the website used and the e-mail address of the seller._

 _These requirements must be fulfilled by the seller of goods (Bolt Market). The law sets no special requirements for the delivery of medicines, however, they must be transported in such a way that does not render them unsuitable for use._

 _We suppose that it is currently impractical for Bolt Market sellers to obtain pharmacy license. However, products like food supplements, bandages, band-aids, pregnancy tests, thermometers and similar may be sold without pharmacy license, so perhaps you might wish looking into this direction. If the product is classified as medical device then additional rules may apply (there are different classes of medical devices, each with different rules), but it would nevertheless be more feasible than a pharmacy license.”_
