To put this into a possible lifecycle example here: 

* A safety ticket arrives for the Spanish market
* *A regular event such as speeding, 1st report* 
* FST creates and completes the tool and admin notes 
* Leaves internal notes for CS to thank the rider for bringing this to our attention
* It automatically populates on a sheet OR a slack channel for OPS teams when Spain is selected 
* FST to leave internal note summarising the event such as “1st report speeding, no block needed” 
* From there OPS will handle all driver comms/calls/blocks all on their own and will handle how they see fit 
* *A significant event comes in such as intoxicated driver*
* FST creates the tool and escalates to our in-house safety team 
* Our team leaves leaves internal notes for CS to thank the rider for bringing this to our attention and we will ensure this matter is resolved 
* It automatically populates on a sheet OR a slack channel for OPS teams when Spain is selected 
* Our in-house team to leave internal note such as “driver’s 1st report of intoxication, no evidence.” Or in another scenario “Driver’s second report of intoxication, a 28-day block recommended” 
* From there OPS will handle all driver comms/calls/blocks all on their own and will handle how they see fit.
* _How does this sound? We can implement this in Estonia as well if is makes sense and if it can easily be automated in the tool._

Hi [~accountid:61138072fc68c100694aed52] 

I have had a quick look at this initiative from a tax perspective. There are no particular show stoppers from a tax perspective, but please see my further comments below:

* Any such referral bonuses are likely to be subject to income tax / business tax (if paid to fleets/registered entrepreneurs) by the recipient in the country of their resident similar to the usual payouts. 
* The reporting of the income and paying the relevant tax in the relevant jurisdiction should be with the recipient of the income, unless the payments are subject to a withholding tax by Bolt in the country of residence of the courier (e.g. likely in EE for couriers that do not have a business account). 
* Such payment will be subject to DAC7 reporting by Bolt Operations OU starting from 1 January 2023, so it’s important that we have a solid overview of these payments and that they will automatically be pulled into the report to be submitted to the Estonian tax authorities. Cc: [~accountid:557058:b2aaf2b9-4465-40fe-b31b-1711dbe61946]  
* Where the courier is registered for VAT, the referral bonus will be subject to VAT. A VAT compliant invoice must be issued by the courier to Bolt Operations (or the local entity where applicable). I understand such invoices are currently manually generated in Portugal. 
* Where the invoice is issued to Bolt Operations OU and the courier is VAT registered in Estonia, the invoice must include a VAT charge of 20% to be paid by Bolt Operations OU, but which will correspondingly be deductible for Bolt Operations OU in Estonia as it is a business related expense. 
* Where the invoice is issued to Bolt Operations OU and the courier is registered outside Estonia, reverse charge of VAT applies (i.e, in broad terms, the courier invoice will show a 0% VAT and Bolt Operations will then report the VAT and make a corresponding deduction in Estonia, so ultimately it should be VAT neutral). However, it’s important that we have this information to submit our VAT returns correctly.    
* I understand the initiative is currently not planned for non-EU countries, but please let me know if you think otherwise. 

If you have any questions, please let me know.

Many thanks

# As a company, are we really okay with 70% of users not getting any clarity about their item and no solution, other than go to the police?
## Yes. This change was driven by the Privacy Team due to heightened privacy concerns around a supervisory authority looking into this issue and safety incidents. At the end of the day, we need to protect rider and driver data, or we risk breaching the GDPR. 
# _CS have to tell the passenger smth like: 'Sorry, we couldn't reach your driver and do not know if he found your item or not”_

## We can remind riders that their items are their responsibility, as per the rider T&Cs. Hey

Comp&Ben has prepared salary ranges globally for all job levels in all job families. We are managing and maintaining one master file: [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1r7M8zn6UXfxBxrbkptUBwbrjYho5_gdK-Rc2LE6xxwQ/edit#gid=1478009508|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1r7M8zn6UXfxBxrbkptUBwbrjYho5_gdK-Rc2LE6xxwQ/edit#gid=1478009508|smart-link] 

This file is used by People Partners and recruitment. It is not shared with managers, because we cannot make all the ranges across all families and levels too available.

Most of these salary ranges have also been uploaded to Workday. For new ranges we either add them manually by ourselves or ask for help with mass upload (happened just once so far prior to salary review in Feb).

The problem however is that there is no clear process for sharing the ranges. The guideline we have set is that Comp&Ben is managing the master file and it is up to People Partners to figure out how their divisions get the data. Logically, the People Partner would need to define what are the needs of the managers they're supporting (who should see what) and then for example create a copy of the ranges file and share it with relevant people and remain responsible for keeping it up to date – that's one option for now but it does work in reality so well.

Our usual suggestion is that each manager can share their own job family and the levels under them (not see their own level and not levels above).

We were hoping that people tech / analytics would be able to figure out some better technical solution here. Some ideas:

# Integrated google sheets so that even though CB team is managing one file, then if we make changes they would automatically appear in other division specific files.
# Workday report which shows the manager all the ranges they need to see, being cautious of not oversharing.

Defining who are the people that should have visibility (who should see what), would still most likely be People Partner's responsibility.

Those are just some ideas, to get better picture we can discuss this further.

Main goal here is to build better technical solution for sharing the salary ranges.
More details here too: [https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C02950DQCEP/p1643548755980089|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C02950DQCEP/p1643548755980089|smart-link] 

Looking forward to your feedback.
Kimberli

I think the attached document describes the message delivery from SNS to the subscriber (SQS in our case); it’s the backoff implementation in case the subscriber cannot receive the messages.
In the original issue, it looks like the consumer gets the message, but it systematically fails to write it into ES, [~accountid:5f770d65837bb800682d18bc] please confirm.

Then, the area of interest is the message lifecycle into AWS SQS architecture.
[https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-basic-architecture.html|https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-basic-architecture.html|smart-link] 


*Important note*

The current NJSC implementation keeps the message{{ in-flight}} in case of error.
Here is the delay in seconds for how long the message stays in-flight up to the next delivery, it’s done by {{changeVisibilityTimeout}} API call.
[https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-nodejs-common/blob/09f25bd480d8a04093bd6d57d11a7db5106d8caf/src/async/mq/subscribe/polling/aws/AwsSqsMqSubscriber.ts#L18|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-nodejs-common/blob/09f25bd480d8a04093bd6d57d11a7db5106d8caf/src/async/mq/subscribe/polling/aws/AwsSqsMqSubscriber.ts#L18]
Although it’s not explicitly named, it’s similar to a backoff retry mechanism backed by a linear function.
As the retry interval is not upper-bounded, the system keeps on retrying up during the message retention period (default = 4 days). 

*Scoping*

* in addition to {{on_error_delay_time_s}}, MQ API could ask for a new added parameter, {{backoff_function}} 
* the {{changeVisibilityTimeout}} should set parameters according with the function
* the upper-bound remains the configured retention period    

E.g.

* {{on_error_delay_time_s: 30s, backoff_function: linear}}

  Delivery Retry: 30s, 60s, 120s … 

* {{on_error_delay_time_s: 2s, backoff_function: exponential}}

Delivery Retry: 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s, 32s
